aboutH2: Dunham House: English-language residential rehab in the Eastern Townships
intro: Dunham House is a residential addiction treatment centre on an 85-acre property in Dunham, in Quebec's Eastern Townships. It treats adults for alcohol and drug addiction, and it specializes in people who also have a mental health condition. Every program runs in English. The centre says that makes it the only English-language dual diagnosis centre in Quebec, and that is the main reason many people from Montreal and the West Island end up here.

It is a registered Canadian charity, started by Daniel Colson after a family member had to go through treatment in a second language. The house holds up to 38 residents, men and women 18 and over, and the centre counts about 800 people treated so far. You can choose a 30-day, 90-day or 6-month stay, and there is an outpatient office in Montreal for the months after.

pillars.title: Eighty-Five Acres Outside Dunham
pillars.body: The campus sits on Chemin Scottsmore, on farmland between Dunham and West Brome in Brome-Missisquoi, with mountains in view. Residents live between the original house and a newer building with its own lounge, gym and counselling rooms. Outside there are walking trails, a pond, a chicken coop and a 7,000 sq. ft. vegetable garden with a greenhouse, and what grows there goes into the meals. People kayak in summer and snowshoe in winter. The horses for equine-assisted learning live at a neighbouring farm a short drive away.

pillars.title: An Outpatient Office in Montreal for the Months After
pillars.body: Most residents come from the Montreal area, so aftercare is based there, at the Queen Elizabeth Health Complex on Marlowe Avenue in NDG. The 12-week outpatient program picks up where residential care ends, and it also takes people who cannot leave home for treatment. Individual counselling is offered in person or remotely and covers gambling, gaming and other compulsive behaviours as well as substances. Peer mentors in the Recovery Transition Program help with housing, work and getting back into the community, and the alumni group keeps meeting long after discharge.

pillars.title: A Clinical Team Backed by McGill Psychiatrists
pillars.body: Clinical director Anthony Berger leads a team of counsellors who, the centre says, all hold at least a bachelor's degree and training in addiction, mental health, social work or somatic work. Psychiatric nurse Brigitte Dubois assesses each resident early on, and Dr. Dominique Desy, the associate physician, can refer people on to a consulting psychiatrist. Two McGill psychiatrists, Dr. Warren Steiner and Dr. Juan Carlos Negrete, have publicly endorsed the program and sit on its advisory board. The kitchen, garden, art, yoga and music staff round out daily life on the campus.

overview: The programs mix structured therapy with time outdoors. Days run six days a week with workshops, lectures and group work, and each resident meets their counsellor every week. The core methods are CBT, DBT, motivational interviewing and relapse prevention, inside a therapeutic community where residents learn from each other. Equine-assisted learning, group music therapy led by an accredited music therapist, pottery and horticultural therapy are part of the week too.

afterOverview: Dunham House is not a detox centre, and people who still need withdrawal management, or who take methadone, have to arrange that first. The 6-month program is subsidized for people who qualify for Quebec social assistance. The 30-day and 90-day programs are private pay, and the centre offers financing through iFinance Medicard. Because it is a charity, donations also fund a sponsorship program for people who fall between public and private care.

location.heading: Dunham House in Dunham, Quebec
location.intro: Dunham House is on Chemin Scottsmore in Dunham, a small town in the Brome-Missisquoi part of the Eastern Townships, about 10 minutes from Cowansville and 20 minutes from Knowlton in Lac-Brome. The centre puts downtown Montreal about an hour and a half away by Autoroute 10, with the South Shore around an hour and 15 minutes, Granby about 30 minutes, Sherbrooke roughly an hour and 15 minutes, and Burlington, Vermont about an hour and a half across the border.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.a: Dunham House treats addiction to alcohol and drugs, and it specializes in people who also live with a mental health condition (dual diagnosis). Addiction is the main focus. When someone needs more mental health care, the on-site psychiatric nurse and general practitioner can refer them to the consulting psychiatrist or to the centre's network of mental health partners.

faqs.q: Are the programs offered in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Dunham House runs all of its programs in English and describes itself as the only English-language centre in Quebec that specializes in dual diagnosis. Residents need to be able to read and understand English.

faqs.q: How long are the residential programs?
faqs.a: There are three residential programs: 30 days, 90 days and 6 months. The 6-month program moves through three phases (stabilization, awareness and an exit plan). The right length is decided during the first assessment, based on your situation.

faqs.q: How much does Dunham House cost, and is it covered?
faqs.a: The centre does not publish a price list and asks you to call admissions, because cost depends on the program and length of stay. The 6-month program is subsidized for people who qualify for Quebec social assistance. The 30-day and 90-day programs are private pay, by cheque, credit card or EFT, and financing is available through iFinance Medicard.

No. Dunham House does not provide detox and cannot admit someone who still needs it, so withdrawal has to be managed before you arrive. The centre also does not accept people on methadone, and its admissions page lists Suboxone as well.

Men and women aged 18 and over with a substance use problem, with or without a mental health condition, who are medically and mentally stable enough to take part in group and individual therapy. Residents must be able to manage daily self-care and climb stairs. The centre also accepts people from outside Quebec and outside Canada.

faqs.q: Where is Dunham House and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The residential campus is at 1964 Chemin Scottsmore in Dunham, in the Brome-Missisquoi part of the Eastern Townships (Cantons-de-l'Est). The centre puts the drive from Montreal at about an hour and a half, mostly along Autoroute 10. Cowansville is about 10 minutes away and Granby about half an hour.

faqs.q: Does Dunham House have services in Montreal?
faqs.a: Yes. Its outpatient office is in the Queen Elizabeth Health Complex at 2100 Marlowe Avenue, Suite 347, in Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It runs a 12-week outpatient program, individual counselling (in person or remote), the family program and peer support for people leaving residential care.

faqs.q: Can family visit, and is there help for families?
faqs.a: Yes. Family members, partners and children can visit on weekends, and staff organize the visits. Dunham House also runs a six-week family program, online or in person in Montreal, on understanding addiction, communication and boundaries.

Admission starts with the online form or a call to 450-263-3434 (option 1). A staff member then calls you back, and the centre says the process usually takes 2 to 4 days, although the waitlist can vary.

faqs.q: Can I bring my phone, and will I share a room?
faqs.a: You can bring a phone, but cell phones, computers and tablets are not used during treatment except in an emergency. The centre has computers and phones on site for contacting family or handling work. Bedrooms hold a maximum of two people.
